workflow.title: Review a Mac cleanup by removal method, not just gigabytes
workflow.primaryIntent: Help Mac owners distinguish app leftovers, duplicates and rebuildable caches before approving cleanup, with CleanMacster's dry run and all-to-Trash setting as the concrete documented example.
workflow.descriptionDirection: A review list is only useful if you know what will be removed and whether it goes to Trash. Separate vendor-documented controls from untested outcomes; never equate selected size with disk space recovered.
outline: After the lead, show the cleared CleanMacster Cleanup app screenshot with version/data caveats, not homepage mock UI.
Inventory item, location and removal method: cache rebuild cost, app support data and personal duplicates need different decisions (C05-C06).
Explain the documented dry run and all-to-Trash switch; contrast with the direct-delete default exception in Terms (C05/S3). No cleanup instructions executed during research.
Treat Full Disk Access and admin prompts as scope changes, not proof an item is disposable (C08).
Use the current-source Breathing Room Space browser preview later, with example-data caption; explain investigation versus deletion without claiming native test results.

Offer one bounded, disclosed decision: CleanMacster for documented app/duplicate workflows and one-time licence; Breathing Room, which we build, for source-implemented app/helper/activity investigation, with preview/runtime/hosted-AI caveats (B01-B02).
workflow.interactionHandoff: A non-destructive checklist of item type, owner, backup/rebuild availability and removal method; no synthetic scanner, default winner or promised savings. Pending implementation in assigned draft scope.
workflow.missingEvidenceRule: Add an official Apple source before asserting general macOS Trash/free-space behavior or an executable step not supported by the retained vendor sources.
